quests.instruction: Two students both want the last red crayon. What is a fair way to solve it?
quests.correctAnswer: Take turns, or one picks another color 🖍️
options: Race to see who can grab it first 🏃
Break the crayon in half to share it 💔
Take turns, or one picks another color 🖍️
quests.hint: Think about how both can be happy.
quests.explanation: Taking turns or switching colors solves the problem without anyone being upset.
quests.funFact: Many conflicts can be solved by finding another way to share.

quests.instruction: A classmate took your pencil without asking. What is a good first step?
quests.correctAnswer: Calmly ask for it back 🗣️
options: Take something of theirs 🔄
Calmly ask for it back 🗣️
Grab it 🫳
quests.explanation: Asking calmly gives them a chance to return it and keeps things peaceful.
quests.funFact: Many people take things by accident without thinking.

quests.instruction: You are getting angry during an argument. What can help?
quests.correctAnswer: Take a deep breath and calm down first 🌬️
options: Say what you think as loudly as you can 📢
Walk away and slam the door behind you 🚪
Take a deep breath and calm down first 🌬️
quests.explanation: Slow breathing helps your body relax so you can think clearly.
quests.funFact: Taking five slow breaths can help your body settle.

quests.instruction: A new classmate speaks a different language at home and is still learning your class language. How can you help them feel welcome?
quests.correctAnswer: Include them and use gestures and pictures 🤝
options: Include them and use gestures and pictures 🤝
Wait until they can speak well to include them 🚪
Speak more loudly so they will understand 📢
quests.explanation: Using gestures and pictures lets them join in while they learn.
quests.funFact: India's constitution officially recognizes 22 languages.

quests.instruction: Your classmates like different games and hobbies. Which attitude is respectful?
quests.correctAnswer: Accept that people like different things 🙂
options: Ask them to change what they like 🔄
Say that your hobby is the best one 🏆
Accept that people like different things 🙂
quests.explanation: Respecting different interests makes it easier to be friends.
quests.funFact: People often learn something new when they try a friend's hobby.

quests.instruction: A classmate gives a wrong answer and others laugh. What can you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Don't laugh; say 'good try' 🙂
options: Don't laugh; say 'good try' 🙂
Laugh along so you fit in 😆
Point out the mistake to the class 📢
quests.explanation: Being kind lets people feel safe to try, and trying is how everyone learns.
quests.funFact: Everyone makes mistakes when learning something new.

quests.instruction: In a relay race, your teammate is slower than expected. What is the best thing to say?
quests.correctAnswer: 'Good effort! We can do it!' 📣
options: 'Good effort! We can do it!' 📣
'You made us lose.' 😠
'I'll never race with you.' 🚫
quests.explanation: Encouraging teammates keeps morale high.
quests.funFact: Relay races have been part of the Olympic Games since 1912.

quests.instruction: Your team loses a game. What shows good sportsmanship?
quests.correctAnswer: Shake hands and say 'well played' 🤝
options: Walk off and don't speak to them 😠
Say the referee made you lose 🧑‍⚖️
Shake hands and say 'well played' 🤝
quests.explanation: Saying 'well played' shows respect for the other team's effort.
quests.funFact: Shaking hands after games is a tradition in many sports.

quests.instruction: In a match, you realize you broke a rule and nobody saw. What is the fair thing to do?
quests.correctAnswer: Admit it and follow the correction ✋
options: Say someone else did it instead 👈
Admit it and follow the correction ✋
Say it didn't happen and play on 🙈
quests.explanation: Admitting a mistake keeps the game fair.
quests.funFact: Fair play is a key idea in the Olympic Games.

quests.instruction: A friend seems sad. Which response shows you noticed and care?
quests.correctAnswer: 'You seem sad. Want to talk?' 💬
options: 'Cheer up! It's not that bad.' 😁
'You seem sad. Want to talk?' 💬
'It's no big deal; forget it.' 🙄
quests.explanation: Asking gently lets your friend share if they want to.
quests.funFact: Noticing feelings is the first step in empathy.

quests.instruction: How can you tell how someone is feeling?
quests.correctAnswer: Notice their face and voice, and kindly ask 👀
options: Guess from the clothes they are wearing 👕
Notice their face and voice, and kindly ask 👀
Ask somebody else to tell you for them 🗣️
quests.hint: People show feelings in many ways.
quests.explanation: Faces, voices, and body language give clues, and asking confirms it.
quests.funFact: People don't always show their feelings in the same way.

quests.instruction: A classmate's pet has died. What is a kind thing to say?
quests.correctAnswer: 'I'm sorry. I'm here if you want to talk.' 💙
options: 'I'm sorry. I'm here if you want to talk.' 💙
'You can get another one soon.' 🐶
'It was only a pet; you'll be fine.' 😒
quests.explanation: Kind words show that you care and are there for them.
quests.funFact: The word 'empathy' comes from a Greek word meaning 'in feeling'.

quests.instruction: During circle time, someone else is speaking and you have an idea. What do you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Wait, then raise your hand ✋
options: Shout out your idea over their voice 📢
Whisper it to your neighbor right away 💬
Wait, then raise your hand ✋
quests.explanation: Waiting for a pause lets everyone hear each speaker.
quests.funFact: Sitting in a circle helps everyone see each other when they talk.

quests.instruction: Many students want to speak in a discussion. What can help it be fair?
quests.correctAnswer: Take turns with a talking object 🔄
options: Take turns with a talking object 🔄
Let the loudest voices speak the most 📢
Let only the teacher talk each time 🧑‍🏫
quests.explanation: A talking object shows whose turn it is, so everyone gets a chance.
quests.funFact: Some classrooms use a ball, stick, or toy as a talking object.

quests.instruction: A classmate shares an idea different from yours. Which response helps the discussion?
quests.correctAnswer: 'What made you think that?' 🤔
options: 'That's a bad idea.' 😒
'What made you think that?' 🤔
Say nothing and roll your eyes 🙄
quests.explanation: A question invites them to share their reasons, so you can both learn.
quests.funFact: Asking 'why' is how people understand each other's ideas.

quests.instruction: You didn't understand a group task, and your teacher is busy. What is a good first step?
quests.correctAnswer: Quietly ask a group member to explain 🙋
options: Copy a friend's work from another group ✏️
Quietly ask a group member to explain 🙋
Wait and say nothing until the end 🤐
quests.explanation: Asking a teammate is a quick way to understand the task.
quests.funFact: Students learning together in pairs is sometimes called peer learning.

quests.instruction: A classmate asks you for help while you're in the middle of work. What is a thoughtful reply?
quests.correctAnswer: 'I'll help you after this part.' 🙂
options: 'I'll help you after this part.' 🙂
'Not now. Ask someone else.' 😒
Say nothing and keep working on it 🤐
quests.explanation: Telling them when you can help is respectful and keeps your work going.
quests.funFact: People appreciate hearing 'later' more than being ignored.

quests.instruction: Your partner explained an answer that seems wrong to you. What can you say?
quests.correctAnswer: 'Can we check it in the book?' 📖
options: 'You're wrong, so I'll change it.' 😠
'I'll just fix it myself later.' 😤
'Can we check it in the book?' 📖
quests.explanation: Checking together turns a disagreement into a way to learn.
quests.funFact: Checking in a trusted book settles many disagreements.

quests.instruction: You said something unkind to a friend. Which is a real apology?
quests.correctAnswer: 'I'm sorry I said that. It wasn't kind.' 🙏
options: 'Sorry that you got upset about it.' 😐
'I'm sorry I said that. It wasn't kind.' 🙏
'Sorry, but you did deserve that.' 😒
quests.hint: A real apology names what you did.
quests.explanation: A real apology says what you did wrong and doesn't blame the other person.
quests.funFact: An apology works best when you mean it.

quests.instruction: After you apologize, what shows you really mean it?
quests.correctAnswer: Changing how you act next time 🔄
options: Saying sorry again many times over 🗣️
Changing how you act next time 🔄
Hoping everyone forgets what happened 🙈
quests.explanation: Changing your behavior shows your apology was sincere.
quests.funFact: People trust apologies backed by actions.

quests.instruction: A classmate says sorry to you. What is a good way to respond?
quests.correctAnswer: 'Thank you for saying sorry.' 🙂
options: 'Thank you for saying sorry.' 🙂
Ignore them 🙈
'I'll never forgive you.' 😠
quests.explanation: Accepting an apology helps repair a friendship.
quests.funFact: In Japanese, there are several ways to say sorry, depending on how serious the situation is.

quests.instruction: Friends dare you to run on the wet floor. What could you say?
quests.correctAnswer: 'No thanks, someone could slip.' 🛑
options: 'Okay, but only one time.' 🚶
'No thanks, someone could slip.' 🛑
'Sure, I'll go first.' 🏃
quests.explanation: Saying no politely keeps you safe, and real friends will respect it.
quests.funFact: Saying no is often easier with a short, calm reason.

quests.instruction: A group is leaving one classmate out on purpose. What is a good choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Include that classmate anyway 🤝
options: Join in so you aren't left out too 🚪
Pretend not to notice what's going on 🙈
Include that classmate anyway 🤝
quests.explanation: Including the classmate shows kindness and may encourage others to do the same.
quests.funFact: One kind act can change how a whole group behaves.

quests.instruction: The group's game is making you feel uneasy. What should you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Walk away and tell a trusted adult 🚶
options: Walk away and tell a trusted adult 🚶
Stay quiet and join in with them 🤐
Record it on a phone to show later 📱
quests.explanation: Leaving and telling an adult keeps you safe and helps stop the problem.
quests.funFact: You never need to join something that feels wrong.

quests.instruction: Someone repeatedly mocks and pushes a classmate to make them feel bad. What is this called?
quests.correctAnswer: Bullying 🚫
options: Bullying 🚫
Teamwork 🤝
Sharing 🎁
quests.hint: It happens again and again and hurts someone.
quests.explanation: Bullying is repeated unkind behavior that hurts another person.
quests.funFact: Bullying can happen in person or online.

quests.instruction: You see a classmate being bullied. What is a good action?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell a teacher and support the classmate 🙋
options: Tell a teacher and support the classmate 🙋
Walk away and say nothing at all 🚶
Laugh along so the bully stays friendly 😆
quests.explanation: Telling an adult gets help, and kindness lets the classmate know they're not alone.
quests.funFact: Many schools have an anti-bullying policy and a person students can report to.

quests.instruction: A bully says, 'Don't tell anyone.' What should you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell a trusted adult anyway 🙋
options: Bully them back so they stop it 👊
Keep it secret as they asked you to 🤐
Tell a trusted adult anyway 🙋
quests.hint: Secrets that hurt should be shared.
quests.explanation: Telling a trusted adult is the right step, even when someone says not to.
quests.funFact: Many schools have a way to report bullying, such as a trusted teacher or a report box.

quests.instruction: You and two friends want different games at break. What is a fair plan?
quests.correctAnswer: Take turns choosing, one game at a time 🔄
options: Skip games and sit out together instead 🪑
Take turns choosing, one game at a time 🔄
Let the tallest friend choose every time 📏
quests.explanation: Taking turns means everyone's choice is played eventually.
quests.funFact: Taking turns is one of the oldest ways of being fair.

quests.instruction: In group work, a teammate is upset because their idea wasn't chosen. What helps?
quests.correctAnswer: Thank them and use a part of their idea 🌟
options: Say their idea can be added next year ⏳
Tell them the idea is already decided 🤫
Thank them and use a part of their idea 🌟
quests.explanation: Including part of their idea helps them feel respected.
quests.funFact: Brainstorming means collecting lots of ideas first and choosing the best afterward.

quests.instruction: A classmate keeps interrupting you. What is a polite way to say it?
quests.correctAnswer: 'I'd like to finish, then I'll listen.' 🗣️
options: 'Be quiet for a minute and let me talk!' 😠
Stop talking and let them go on 🤐
'I'd like to finish, then I'll listen.' 🗣️
quests.explanation: Politely asking to finish speaks up for yourself without being rude.
quests.funFact: Using 'I' sentences helps people listen.
